definitions.explanation: Having lived or existed for a short time. Used for people and sometimes animals.
Can also describe someone who acts or looks young, or is inexperienced.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{若|わか}いです。
{若|わか}い{時|とき}、たくさん{本|ほん}を{読|よ}みました。
examples.english: When I was young, I read a lot of books.

examples.japanese: あの{先生|せんせい}はまだ{若|わか}いですが、とても{上手|じょうず}です。
examples.english: That teacher is still young, but very skilled.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}の{祖父|そふ}は{八十歳|はちじゅっさい}ですが、{心|こころ}は{若|わか}いです。{毎日|まいにち}{散歩|さんぽ}しています。
examples.english: My grandfather is 80 years old, but he is young at heart. He walks every day.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}はよく{運動|うんどう}した。
examples.english: When I was young, I used to exercise a lot.

examples.japanese: {若者|わかもの}に{人気|にんき}がある。
まだ{若|わか}いから、{失敗|しっぱい}してもいい。
examples.english: It's okay to fail because you're still young.

notes:
USAGE:
{若|わか}い is primarily used for people and living things, while {新|あたら}しい is used for objects and things.

COMPOUNDS:
- {若者|わかもの}: young person, youth
- {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}/{若|わか}い{時|とき}: when (one was) young
- {若手|わかて}: young (talent/employee)
- {若葉|わかば}: young leaves, fresh greenery

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {若|わか}く{見|み}える: to look young (a common compliment)
- {気|き}が{若|わか}い: young at heart
- {考|かんが}えが{若|わか}い: immature thinking (slightly negative)
